answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when reputation is earned like a glacier carving a valley: slowly, through verified work that cannot be faked in bulk. Newcomers lock a refundable stake, then complete small tasks checked by randomly assigned peers, earning signed receipts hash-chained to the previous one. Trust accrues only from that ledger, so the horizon of full participation stays far from anyone with no verified history, while the haven of trusted transacting opens only to identities whose receipts prove real output. One forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the deposit.
